bull.b: The sharp year-over-year improvement in revenue and quarterly net income indicates stronger monetization from the current portfolio, particularly ARK content and Bellwright. If supported by continued releases, this rebound could improve operating leverage and provide greater capacity to fund future development.

A broad multi-year pipeline gives Snail multiple opportunities to extend established franchises while introducing new content and tools. Regular DLC and new-title launches can support recurring engagement, diversify release timing, and reduce reliance on a single quarter’s product slate.

High unit sales and daily user activity demonstrate meaningful customer engagement in Snail’s principal franchise. A large active community can support ongoing downloadable-content monetization, strengthen the value of future updates, and provide a durable base for recurring live-operations revenue.

bear.b: Negative equity and meaningful debt materially reduce financial flexibility and leave less balance-sheet capacity to absorb weaker releases or fund development internally. The deterioration from positive equity in 2024 also signals that restoring capital strength remains a central requirement for stability.

Unreliable operating and free cash flow makes it harder for Snail to consistently finance content development from its own operations. Repeated negative periods can increase dependence on external funding or portfolio timing, limiting resilience when launches underperform or expenses rise.

The conditional listing exception creates an ongoing corporate constraint tied directly to the company’s weak equity position. Failure to restore and sustain the required threshold could lead to delisting, potentially disrupting market access and complicating future capital-raising efforts.
